items.problem: Bootstrap omitted externally linked UWP project inputs and forced incomplete manual shell reconstruction.
items.evidence: lessons.json dev_agent_struggles[0]; skill-defects.json items[0]; session-log.txt mapping contained 5 local files while OCR.csproj linked 15 shared inputs.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 enumerated only files physically under -Source and did not follow MSBuild Include + Link metadata.
items.change: Resolve common legacy MSBuild properties, copy linked Compile/ApplicationDefinition/Page/Content inputs to safe target-relative Link paths, include them in mapping/TODO processing, and stop on unresolved links.
items.expected_effect: Shared App.xaml, shell, styles, helpers, and assets enter the normal mechanical migration path instead of being selectively recreated.
items.falsifiable_check: Running bootstrap on the OCR source reports 15 externally linked inputs, maps MainPage.xaml and Styles\Styles.xaml, and preserves App.xaml RequestedTheme="Dark".

items.problem: Incorrect/unclear command and API guidance caused a failed build command, orientation/lifecycle compile errors, and stale references after a control swap.
items.evidence: skill-defects.json command/display/lifecycle items, skill-coverage-gaps.json items[1], and lessons.json errors for winapp build, DisplayInformation, Suspending/Resuming, and PreviewControl.
items.root_cause: The skill prescribed a nonexistent build subcommand, overstated the Windows App SDK DisplayInformation surface, omitted suspend/resume subscription migration, and contradicted itself about preserving versus renaming CaptureElement.
items.change: Use dotnet build consistently, correct DisplayInformation capability mapping, add explicit page/window lifetime guidance, and require a scoped old-name search after element swaps.
items.expected_effect: Agents avoid a guaranteed failed command and nonexistent display/lifecycle members, then finish all references when replacing XAML controls.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, compilation starts with dotnet build and no CS1061/CS0103 errors mention DisplayInformation orientation, Application Suspending/Resuming, or the replaced preview element name.
items.tier_justification: These replacements depend on whether code needs color, scale, physical orientation, page lifetime, or window lifetime; a mechanical rewrite would silently change behavior, so focused decision guidance is safer than Tier 1/2 automation.

items.problem: Both scored features changed from the source's dark/lightweight presentation to light/bold WinUI defaults.
items.evidence: migration-score.json marks both features partial; discrepancies.json records two major visual differences; source SharedContent/xaml/App.xaml has RequestedTheme="Dark" and the target omitted it.
items.root_cause: Fidelity prose emphasized element preservation but did not explicitly protect root theme metadata or effective values inherited from platform styles/resources.
items.change: Promote RequestedTheme, explicit visual properties, and effective inherited typography/brush values to fidelity invariants in SKILL.md and the XAML pattern.
items.expected_effect: Migrations preserve source theme and pin values where same-named WinUI defaults render differently.
items.falsifiable_check: On re-run, App.xaml retains RequestedTheme="Dark" and both OCR features no longer receive the light/bold visual discrepancy.
items.tier_justification: Static tooling can preserve explicit metadata but cannot infer whether two framework styles have equivalent rendered semantics across theme, state, DPI, and OS versions; the agent must compare intent/effective values.
